fact_text: Pakistan Oilfields' largest producing field is the Tal block, where OGDC and PPL are also partners, so the company's main output sits in a jointly held field.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Crude oil supplies most of Pakistan Oilfields' revenue; crude goes to refineries and then to fuel pumps that pay cash, so oil receivables are rarely stuck in the chain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local crude prices are set under successive petroleum policies (1994, 1997, 2001, 2012) that link them to international crude, net of royalties and windfall levies whose rates differ by policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A windfall levy takes a share of the extra revenue when international crude rises, so a local producer gains less from a crude price rally than the headline price suggests.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 2001 petroleum policy capped the gas price paid to local producers at a maximum of USD 3.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 2012 petroleum policy raised the maximum gas price for local producers to USD 6, roughly double the 2001 ceiling.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 12.5% royalty applies to upstream oil and gas production in Pakistan, and the producer's costs are taken out after it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Circular debt is the sector's central payment risk: it delays government payments to large upstream producers, and the analyst sees the big state-owned producers as hit hardest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan Oilfields has so far avoided circular-debt delays on gas because its gas is a small share of national output, letting it collect from the gas utility on time.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: OGDC and PPL each produce a large share of national gas, so they cannot escape a country-wide circular debt, and their government-appointed management is unlikely to retaliate against state pricing policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst contrasts Pakistan Oilfields with the government-owned OGDC and PPL: its management is not government-appointed, so it can take a harder line on payments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Management's phrase that it only does clean business is read as a signal it would cut production if payments are not collected, which is a lever against circular debt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Furnace oil use in the power sector caused circular debt on the oil side in the past; since furnace oil use ended, the analyst sees the oil side as largely free of that problem.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Short reserve life in the main fields is the company's biggest risk, but upward reserve revisions and new discoveries can keep reserves replacing production.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Recent discoveries in the Rajgir, Makri Deep and Ikhlas blocks could add to output and help keep production stable as older fields mature.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fixed-volume LNG contracts cut local gas demand, which forces gas output to be curtailed; oil from the same wells is curtailed too, because the two come out together.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Qatar LNG contract allows price and volume renegotiation after its first ten years, a clause that could ease the gas oversupply and the curtailment it causes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan Oilfields belongs to the Attock group, which the analyst says could consider selling its Pakistan holdings, making a sale of POL a possible catalyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 2021 deal in which a Hub Power subsidiary bought an international oil company's Pakistan unit is cited as a precedent; Pakistan Oilfields produces about ten times that unit's output.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An exploration company with a short reserve life deserves a lower P/E; continued discoveries that replace production can move its multiple toward the market P/E.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan Oilfields is in litigation from 2018 at the Islamabad High Court over whether a gas pricing policy extended to oil; meanwhile it records the disputed revenue at the old rates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A favourable court verdict would let the company book the disputed extra gas revenue in one lump sum, a one-time upside to earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For FY26 the analyst assumes revenue of roughly PKR 65-70 billion on average output of about 4,500 barrels of oil a day and about 50 MMCFD of gas.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For FY26 the analyst estimates profit before tax near PKR 50 billion and profit after tax near PKR 30 billion, after royalties, operating costs and tax.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For FY26 the analyst's per-share estimate is EPS of roughly PKR 100-110, with a generous dividend policy supporting a dividend of about PKR 80-90 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sees the stock's earnings as favourable while crude stays roughly in the USD 75-80 range; above about USD 90-100 the weaker economy and market sentiment outweigh the gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Very high crude prices hurt the wider economy: they raise interest-rate risk and push down the market P/E, which weighs on minority shareholders even of oil producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Dividend King of Oil & Gas - Everything You Need to Know About Pakistan Oilfields' (YouTube transcript, undated)
